title: Select [CASE WHEN]
description:
## CASE WHEN
CASE WHEN is if/else inside SQL. It creates a new value based on conditions.
```sql
SELECT name,
    CASE
        WHEN uptime > 95 THEN 'healthy'
        WHEN uptime > 50 THEN 'degraded'
        ELSE 'critical'
    END as health
FROM servers;
```
This checks each row and assigns a label based on the condition. `END` closes the CASE block. `as health` names the new column.

---
## Assignment:
BWS needs a server report. Select each server's name and a priority label:
- cpu_cores >= 8 -> 'high'
- cpu_cores >= 4 -> 'medium'
- everything else -> 'low' as priority
setupCode: CREATE TABLE servers (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, cpu_cores INTEGER, status TEXT); INSERT INTO servers VALUES (1, 'prod-1', 8, 'running'), (2, 'prod-2', 16, 'running'), (3, 'staging-1', 4, 'stopped'), (4, 'dev-box', 2, 'on fire'), (5, 'test', 1, 'pending');
expectedOutput:
name | priority
prod-1 | high
prod-2 | high
staging-1 | medium
dev-box | low
test | low
